cipher.name: AlternatingCaseAtbash
cipher.idea: A variation of the Atbash cipher that alternates between standard Atbash substitution and a fixed shift of 5 positions depending on the character's index in the string. This introduces a position-dependent element to break simple frequency analysis while remaining highly intuitive and easy for language models to compute accurately. Non-alphabetic characters are left unchanged and do not advance the index counter.
cipher.encrypt_rules: For each alphabetic character in the plaintext, determine its 0-based index among only the alphabetic characters processed so far. If the index is even, apply the standard Atbash cipher (A<->Z, B<->Y, etc., preserving case). If the index is odd, shift the character forward by 5 positions in the alphabet (A->F, B->G, etc., wrapping around from Z to A, preserving case). Non-alphabetic characters (spaces, punctuation, digits) are kept exactly as they are and do not count toward the index.
cipher.decrypt_rules: For each alphabetic character in the ciphertext, determine its 0-based index among only the alphabetic characters processed so far. If the index is even, apply the standard Atbash cipher (Z<->A, Y<->B, etc., preserving case). If the index is odd, shift the character backward by 5 positions in the alphabet (F->A, G->B, etc., wrapping around from A to Z, preserving case). Non-alphabetic characters are kept exactly as they are and do not count toward the index.
